title: Market Survey for the followings part numbers- S007250, S007251, S007252, and S007260 � associated with the Black Hornet (BH4) Unmanned Aircraft.
description: Sources sought to provide the government with the unmanned Aircraft ( 1550-25-163-7663), Unmanned Aircraft Main Module (1550-25-163-7895); Grip Assembly, Controller AC ( 1680-25-163-7661), and Case, Electronic Communication (Hangar) ( 5895-25-163-7662, for the U.S. Military. The AN/ZSH-3(V)1 Black Hornet 4 (BH4) is a soldier Borne Sensor (SBS) designed specifically for dismounted Operators. It provides lower echelon units with an organic and immediate capability for enhancing situational awareness with minimal increase in equipment volume and weight. Requirements Description: The United States Army is looking for sources with the ability to provide the S007250 Unmanned Aircraft Vehicle (1550-25-163-7663), S007251 Unmanned Aircraft Main Module (1550-25-163-7895), S007260 Grip Assembly Controller AC (1680-25-163-7661), and the S007252 Case, Electronic Communication (Hangar) (5895-25-163-7262) for the AN/ZSH-3(V)1 BH4. The Government requires an estimated quantity of 2,300 S007250, 1,100 S007251, 750 S007260, and 550 S007252 over a 3-year period. This is not a solicitation. This is only an estimate and will not bind the contractor or the Government in any way or at any time into a contract with any of the specified terms below. Suppliers capable of supplying these items, in accordance with the government data package and in the quantities specified above, should contact the government before October 16, 2026. Submissions can be sent to michelet.audige.civ@army.mil. Responses must include a list of items the supplier is able to produce or source as well as documentation that the supplier can provide the army with a physically and functionally component from the list above. Examples of such documentation can be test results, copy of purchase orders if the supplier was a vendor to the listed source, or a statement from listed source demonstrating that the supplier can provide the Army a solution. For more information contact Michelet Audige at michelet.audige.civ@army.mil. At a minimum the support information you submit should include, but is not limited to, the following types of documentation: Questionnaire, information on previous Government and commercial contracts, and evidence that the item can be provided. In your response, please include your company name, CAGE code, and a technical point of contact with email address and telephone number. Notice, Response Due Date, and Points of Contact: This is NOT a Request for Quote or Proposal. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this SSA or reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses to this SSA. title: Pumping Assembly, Water
description: ** NOTE **: The below questions and answers regarding the Publications and Packaging CDRL portions of the solicitation are posted here for your reference: Packaging - Attachment 15 Question(s) 1. Section F calls out preserving all exterior unpainted metal surfaces in accordance with MIL-STD-2073 and coating said surfaces with preservative MIL-PRF-16173, Grade 1. In MIL-PRF-53051D, Section 3.10, it states that CARC paint shall not be applied to surfaces greater than 400F which means our metallic exhaust guard would not be painted. Is this coating able to be applied to surfaces greater than 400F? Additionally, is there a reason that preservative MIL-PRF-16173, Grade 1 is not listed in MIL-PRF-53051D anywhere? 2. Is there a MIL, ISO, FDA or some other standard that the corrosion preventative coating for food handling machinery and equipment must meet? Additionally, why is this not a requirement for the Type II - Pump Assembly, Water in MIL-PRF-53051D? The SPI calls out a preservative that can be used on bare metal when the item is in storage to prevent corrosion. I�m not sure where MIL-PRF-53051D is coming from, it maybe from the PD, which would be engineering and could be focusing on the inside of the pump. If the contractor wants to use a different preservative on non-metal, it will need to be from MIL-STD-2073, Appendix J and that preservative would need to meet the functionality of MIL-PRF-016173. 3. As far as the packaging preservative goes, these systems are painted with Chemical Agent Resistant Coating (CARC) which has anti-corrosive properties already in it as called out in MIL-PRF-53051D which is the MIL-PRF that these systems are manufactured too. Additionally, they are required based on the solicitation to be delivered in heat treated wooden crates. Is the packaging team stating that the preservative needs to be applied to the wooden crate or the exterior of the unit? The internals of the pump system are already cast aluminum and stainless steel which are inherently corrosion resistant.� I�m not seeing where MIL-PRF-53051D was listed in packaging. I reviewed the pkg contract language and CDRLs and didn�t see where it was mentioned. Did the contractor see that in the Purchase Description? If so, that would be an engineering question to answer. As far as the wooden crate, it needs to follow heat treatment requirements per DOD 4140.65M and the requirements of the International Standards for Phytosanitary Measures 15 (ISPM), Regulation of Wood Packaging Material as laid out in Section D of the contract. *** Amendment 0005 is issued to extend the proposal due date out to 16 Oct 2026, change the FOB point from Origin to Destination for the production CLINs, revise the Section C Statement of Work (SOW) to remove references to Provisioning, Publications, and Technical Manuals, revise the list of addenda and attachments in Section J, remove select CDRLs and attachments as required, add a CDRL for a Commercial Off-the Shelf (COTS) Operator's Manual in Section J for government review prior to approval, and add/delete or update any clauses or provisions as required (especially due to the revolutionary FAR overhaul). *** Amendment 0004 is issued to extend the proposal due date out to 05 Dec 2025 *** *** Amendment 0003 is issued to extend the proposal due date out to 21 Nov 2025 *** *** Amendment 0002 is issued to extend the proposal due date out to 31 Oct 2025 *** *** Amendment 0001 is issued to extend the proposal due date out to 10 Oct 2025 *** Item: Pumping Assembly, Water NSN: 4320-01-691-1630 P/N: M53051-2-2 (CAGE 81349, Government) Qty: 14 each basic, 14 each option Packaging: Military A FOB: Destination Contract Type: Definitive contract with 100% option for 365 days Notes: This procurement is established as a 100% Total Small Business SetAside. First Article Testing (FAT) is required (provision for FAT waiver is allowed) and Government approval must be obtained prior to manufacturing the production quantity. Part number M53051-2-2 (Water Pump, 600 GPM) is built utilizing the standards listed in MIL-PRF-53051D (dated 20 Apr 2022). A copy of the MIL-PRF is attached in the Pre-Solicitation notice for this opportunity. The solicitation includes a Statement of Work (SOW) in Section C, with a list of packaging data, safety/security and hazardous material data required by the Government. These details are listed on the solicitation as narratives, Contract Data Requirements List (CDRLs) and attachments. There are 7 CDRLs and 7 attachments that support the CDRLs. Thoroughly review the solicitation document and amendments for all requirements prior to submitting your proposal. ***** Contact the Contract Specialist to obtain all of the CDRL and attachment documentation via the DoD Safe Site. *****

Space must be located in a prime commercial office district with attractive surroundings with a prevalence of modern design and/or tasteful rehabilitation in modern use. Space shall be located in a professional office setting and preferably not within close proximity to residential areas, railroad tracks or power transmission lines. Through its automation capabilities, configurable data models, and audit?ready workflow and trail features, the platform has improved accuracy, reduced cycle time, and strengthened transparency in FirstNet Authority�s financial planning and reporting activities. These capabilities represent the core functionality FirstNet Authority has implemented to date, which has formed the foundation for FirstNet Authority�s ongoing transformation toward more efficient and reliable enterprise financial management. title: Dworshak Powerhouse Roof Replacement
description: Title: Dworshak Powerhouse Roof Replacement: The work is located at the Dworshak Powerhouse, Ahsahka, Idaho. The solicitation will be issued as an Invitation for Bid (IFB) and result in a single firm-fixed price construction contract. This procurement is unrestricted. Competition is open to both large and small business concerns. A small business subcontracting plan is required for large businesses. 100% performance and payment bonds will be required for this project. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS code for this project is 238160 Roofing Contractors, and the associated small business size standard is $19 million in average annual receipts. Solicitation number W912EF27BA001 will be posted to the SAM.gov Contract Opportunities website on or about mid to late October 2026. The bid due date will be contained in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments that may be issued. The solicitation will be made available for download on the SAM.gov Contract Opportunities website. Offerors are responsible for checking the referenced page for any updates to the Notice. The Government is not responsible for any loss of Internet connectivity or for an offeror's inability to access the documents posted at the referenced website. Bids will be due approximately 30 days after the solicitation is posted. The exact proposal due date will be indicated in the solicitation. System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors must register in the SAM at https://sam.gov/content/home prior to receiving an award. NOTE: The response date that is required to post this notice is not in any way a due date for any submission. This is a pre-solicitation notice only. Scope: The scope of the work is to provide a durable waterproofing system for the Dworshak powerhouse and ancillary roofs. This will be achieved by removing the existing roofing system in its entirety down to the structural roof decks, followed by the installation of a new fully adhered roofing assembly to include gypsum roof sheathing, a vapor retarder, polyisocyanurate foam roof insulation, cover board, and 90-mil EPDM membrane. A 2-year installer warranty and a 30-year manufacturer warranty are required. Fall protection guardrails constructed from fiber-reinforced plastic (FRP) will be installed to the parapet walls of the powerhouse and elevator penthouse roofs to ensure a safe work environment for maintenance personnel conducting preventative maintenance activities on the roofs. Fabricated metal stairs will be installed to replace existing ladder access to two roof areas. The mechanical air conditioning unit for the elevator machine room will be replaced with a new split heat pump system with indoor air handler and outdoor condenser unit. Roof parapet heights above the parking lot/roadway range from 36 feet high to 75 feet high. Cranes and/or telescopic boom lifts will be necessary to deliver material on to the roof surfaces. High voltage equipment and overhead transmission lines will limit placement and reach of equipment. Demolished materials may be removed using cranes, telescopic boom lifts, or debris chutes. THE GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO CANCEL THE SOLICITATION EITHER BEFORE OR AFTER THE CLOSING DATE. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUEST. All on-site work shall be performed in accordance with the Corps of Engineers Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1). Establish and manage an effective on-site Safety and Health program in accordance with EM 385-1-1 that will require the development and submission of a comprehensive project specific Accident Prevention Plan for Government acceptance. In addition, develop and submit for Government acceptance Activity Hazard Analyses for each phase of work and a project specific Fall Protection Plan that comply with EM 385-1-1. A Site Safety and Health Officer (SSHO) employed by the prime contractor is required for each shift of the contractor's on-site operations. The SSHO shall possess a minimum of 5-years� experience in construction safety on similar projects, shall have completed the 30-Hour OSHA Construction Safety training within the last 5 years, and shall have completed at least 24 hours of safety training from accredited safety training sources each year for the past 5 years. Establish and manage an effective Contractor Quality Control (CQC) System that will require the development and submission of a comprehensive project specific CQC Plan for Government acceptance. A CQC System Manager employed by the prime contractor is required to be on-site for each shift of the Contractor's operations. The CQC System Manager must possess a minimum of 5 years relevant experience in a supervisory or management position such as Quality Control Manager, Quality Assurance Manager, or Construction Manager directly involved in the management of construction quality at the project site. In addition, the CQC System Manager shall have completed the course entitled �Construction Quality Management for Contractors� within the last 5 years. Use the Government-furnished Resident Management System (RMS) � Contractor Mode to record, maintain, and submit various information throughout the contract period. RMS is a Windows-based program capable of operating on a stand-alone personal computer or on a network. The Government will make the quality control system (QCS) software available to the Contractor at time of notice to proceed. The project involves the development and management of Contractor furnished submittals for items such as pre-construction plans, product data, test reports, and contract close-out documentation as required by the technical specifications of the contract. Miscellaneous work within the project includes the delivery of As-Built Drawings, O&M Manuals, Contractor- Prepared Shop Drawings, and spare parts to the customer. Solicitation Number W912EF27BA001 will be posted to the SAM.gov approximately on around mid to late October 2026. The solicitation is a Request for Proposal Important Note: The SAM.gov Contract Opportunities Response Date listed elsewhere in this synopsis is for SAM.gov archive purposes only. It does not necessarily reflect the actual bid opening date. There is no response date included in this notice. The bid due date and time will be contained in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments that are issued. Anticipated Award date is January 2027. A site visit will be offered approximately 2 weeks after the solicitation is made available to offerors. See solicitation for details about the site visit. ACCESS FOR FOREIGN NATIONALS: Security clearance for foreign nationals to attend a site visit requires approximately 4 weeks; therefore, clearance should be requested immediately. To request clearance, please submit the names of all foreign nationals proposed for site visit attendance, along with documentation to verify that he/she was legally admitted into the United States and has authority to work and/or go to school in the US. Such documentation may include a US passport, Certificate of US citizenship (INS Form N-560 or N-561), Certificate of Naturalization (INS Form N-550 or N-570), foreign passport with 1-551 stamp or attached INS Form 1-94 indicating employment authorization, Alien Registration Receipt Card with photograph (INS Form 1-151 or 1-551), Temporary Resident Card (INS Form 1-688}, Employment Authorization Card (INS Form l-688A}, Reentry Permit (INS Form 1-327}, Refugee Travel Document (INS Form 1-571}, Employment Authorization Document issued by the INS which contains a photograph (INS Form I-688B}. Send this information by email to leanne.r.walling@usace.army.mil and Cynthia.h.jacobsen@usace.army.mil Foreign nationals must have received clearance prior to being granted access to the project site.

title: Future Submarine Digital Backbone Industry Day
description: Industry Day: Future Submarine Digital Backbone Registration Required by October 16, 2026 Director, Submarine Programs (DSP) seeks industry input regarding the future submarine digital backbone. The Director, Design & Construction (D,D&C) within Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager, Submarines (DRPM Subs) will host a one-day classified Industry Day on November 18, 2026 (9:00 AM EST) at Systems Planning and Analysis (SPA), 2001 N Beauregard St., Alexandria, VA 22311. This event will focus on using digital design in submarine acquisition. Industry input and engagement is needed to turn this plan into executable tasking. The meeting will be held at the SECRET level. Future submarines need a digital backbone that enables maximum system interconnectivity, centralized data storage, and future extensibility. Sustainment, operations, logistics, and condition-based maintenance must be enabled by the Common Computing Environment (CCE). Future submarines require state-of-the-art Data Center technology in a submarine environment, accounting for space, weight, power, and cooling constraints as well as militarization of the technology. This future state also includes connectivity of systems that have not previously been networked. DSP is seeking specific technical solutions and concepts from industry to support the following areas: Software Defined Architecture Common Computing Environment / Data Center Technology Modular Open Systems Architecture (MOSA) Submarine Systems User Needs Hull, Mechanical, & Electrical (HM&E) Systems Agenda Morning Session: The first half of the day will consist of the Government briefing attendees on SSN(X) objectives, schedule, and requirements development, the drivers for a future submarine digital backbone, user needs, and the vision for a submarine platform-wide common computing environment. Afternoon Session: The second half of the day will consist of scheduled one-on-one sessions with the Government, shipbuilders, and UARCs present, allowing Industry to present technical solutions and ideas for the future submarine digital backbone. Note: Do not submit generic capability statements. DSP is only seeking specific technical solutions and ideas for future submarine digital backbone solutions. Attendance & Capacity Limits Due to limited capacity, attendance is limited to two (2) individuals per company/organization to participate in-person for the event, with exceptions granted solely for designated presenters approved in advance by the PMS 351 Program Office. Foreign nationals are not allowed to attend. No virtual option is available for this event. Clearance Verification: All attendees must be U.S. citizens and possess a final, active U.S. SECRET (or higher) security clearance. Interim clearances will not be accepted for facility access. Contractual Disclaimer This notice is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP) and the Government is not requesting or accepting proposals currently. No awards will be made from this announcement. This announcement is not requesting any materials from interested parties. The Government will not reimburse for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement. The Government also will not reimburse any costs related to a party�s participation and attendance of the event. REGISTRATION PROCESS (TWO-STEP VERIFICATION) To participate in this event, companies must complete both of the following steps by 16 October: Step 1: Email Registration Email the PMS 351 Industry Engagement Inbox at pms351industry@us.navy.mil with the subject line �DSP Digital Backbone Industry Day Registration � [Company Name]. In this email, please provide Primary Point of Contact (Name, Title Email, Phone Number) Company/Organization Name, CAGE Code, and Address Names, titles, email addresses, and clearance status of the participating individuals (maximum of 2 per company) Statement indicating whether a 1-on-1 session is requested Step 2: DISS VAR Submission A formal VAR must be submitted via the Defense Information System for Security (DISS). Host Facility: SPA SPA SMO Code: 7L563 Purpose of Visit: DRPM Subs / DSP Future Submarine Digital Backbone Industry Day Point of Contact: Mr. Joshua Engle (joshua.engle@spa.com or 571-771-0859) Date of Visit: November 18, 2026 Note: VARs must be received and verified in DISS no later than October 19, 2026. Attendees without an approved VAR in DISS will be denied entry to the SPA facility FACILITY RULES & SECURITY PROTOCOLS Identification: Each attendee must present a valid, unexpired U.S. government-issued photo ID (e.g., CAC, Military ID, or U.S. Passport) at the check-in desk. Prohibited Devices: SPA is a classified facility. Absolutely no electronic devices, wearable technology, or recording-capable hardware will be permitted inside the briefing or breakout rooms. This includes, but is not limited to: Mobile phones and tablets Smartwatches and fitness trackers (e.g., Apple Watch, Fitbit) Laptops and electronic storage media (USBs, external hard drives) Cameras, voice recorders, and Bluetooth-enabled devices Smart Glasses Storage: Limited secure storage lockboxes may be available at the facility entrance, but attendees are highly encouraged to leave prohibited electronic devices in their vehicles. Note: Bluetooth enabled medical devices must be approved by SPA Security prior to arrival � please email device type & model number to Samuel.sangobowale@spa.com & mkinney@spa.com by November 6, 2026.

title: Z2DA--FY27 NRM RENOVATE SURGICAL SUITE PHASE II
description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE 658-19-103 Renovate Surgical Suite Phase II Salem VA Medical Center (Salem, Virginia) The Department of Veterans Affairs, Salem VA Medical Center in Salem, Virginia, has a requirement for a contractor to provide construction services to complete Project 658-19-103 Renovate Surgical Suite Phase II in accordance with the solicitation and any resulting contract. DESCRIPTION: Project 658-19-103 Renovate Surgical Suite Phase II: This construction services project includes general construction, structural, architectural, fire suppression, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and fire alarm systems trades to perform work in Building 143 at the Salem VA Medical Center. The purpose of the project is to expand and renovate an existing surgical suite to comply with the current VA design guidelines and provide innovative functional spaces. This requirement corrects several outstanding deficiencies discovered during the facilities condition assessment (FCA) as a result of obsolete equipment and infrastructure for surgical services per the VA Design Manual and other dictating medical codes. The project will be broken down into four phases with each phase being completed and activated prior to the next phase beginning. The first phase will consist of creating three new operating rooms in a currently vacant area of the hospital, resulting in no impact to operating room functions. The second phase will include complete renovation of the existing operating rooms, and patients will be re-routed to the new operating rooms constructed during the first phase. Phase three will include the nursing station pre-op area. This is not expected to impact patient care as alternative areas nearby will be used for post-op. The final phase includes what is currently the post-op recovery and surgical area. The place of performance is the Salem VA Medical Center at 1970 Roanoke Blvd. Salem VA 24153. The period of performance for this project is 840 calendar days from the issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP). MAGNITUDE OF CONSTRUCTION: Between $20,000,000 and $30,000,000. The NAICS code for this action is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (SBA Size Standard: $45.0m annual revenue). The Product Service Code is Z2DA, Repair or Alteration of Hospitals and Infirmaries. UNRESTRICTED SOLICITATION: The solicitation being issued will be Unrestricted without any set-aside. Only one award will be made. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be made available on or around Friday, October 16, 2026. The solicitation and any amendments will be posted on this website, www.sam.gov, Contract Opportunities. The solicitation will include instructions to offerors/bidders. title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO RENEW OFFICE LEASE - WYNNE, AR
description: SOLICITATON FOR OFFER LOCATION: Wynne, AR The U.S. Government currently occupies office and storage space in a building under lease that will be expiring. The Government is considering alternate space if economically advantageous. In making this determination, the government will consider, among other things, the availability of alternate space that potentially can satisfy the government's requirements, as well as costs likely to be incurred through relocating, such as physical move costs, replication of tenant improvements and telecommunication infrastructure, and non-productive agency downtime. The Government's desire is for a full service lease for approximately 5,000 rentable square feet of office space for an U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Area Office, for a term not to exceed five (5) years with Government termination rights and located with a defined delineated area; Near or within a 15-mile radius of Wynne, AR 72396. Exclusive on-site secure parking for (9) government vehicles must be provided on a 24 hour 7 days a week basis. Offered space must meet Government requirements per the terms of the Government Lease. Interested respondents may include building owners and representatives with the exclusive right to represent building owners. Representatives of building owners must include the exclusivity agreement, representation letter, listing contract or other executed agreement granting exclusive right to represent the building owner with their response to this solicitation. Additional information regarding this solicitation may be obtained from Monalisa Zewatski by email at Monalisa.C.Zewatski@usace.army.mil. Proposals are due no later than 5:30 pm on 10/16/2026. Lease documents are attached.

title: Z--Laboratory Facility Operation & Maintenance
description: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 7, Acquisition Management Branch, is seeking the services of an experienced firm to provide Facility Operations and Maintenance services for the U.S. EPA Region 10 Manchester Laboratory, 7411 Beach Dr. East, Port Orchard, WA, which provides chemical analysis; microbiological analyses; whole effluent toxicity; method development and other applied science activities; design consultation for environmental projects; and other related activities. The R10 Manchester Laboratory complex is comprised of multiple buildings in which all buildings are single story occupancy with some mechanical spaces on a second floor or mezzanine. Buildings are clustered near one another on a 17.5-acre site, including approximately 3 acres of landscaped areas, and 3 acres of paved areas and roadway. This facility houses approximately 85 federal, state and contract employees. The work to be performed under this contract consists of continuous service of its mechanical systems with little or no breakdowns; effective maintenance to ensure facility preservation; and efficient operation of systems and equipment. Additional services may be ordered at the discretion of the Government for work relating to the operations, maintenance and repair or upgrade of the covered facilities, but not covered in the basic monthly services of the contract. The Period of Performance (POP) for this procurement will be one (1) Base Period and four (4) Option Periods. Estimated dollar value for this procurement is between $5M - $8M. This procurement will be a total Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business set-aside. The RFP is anticipated to be issued on or about 10/16/2026 and will be posted on the System for Award Management (SAM) website (www.sam.gov) and the FedConnect website (www.fedconnect.net).

title: Denmark – Construction work – Løvbakkernes Vandværk
description: Ordregiver udbyder en totalentreprisekontrakt vedrørende projektering, opførelse og idriftsættelse af Løvbak-kernes Vandværk nord for Herning. Vandværk placeres på matrikel nr. 1r, Gullestrup, Herning Jorder. Det nye vandværk skal have en produktionskapacitet på 3 millioner m³/år, med mulighed for udvidelse til 4,5 millioner m³/år efter 2040. Hovedformålet med det nye vandværk er at sikre fremtidens produktion af drikkevand og højne Herning Vands forsyningssikkerhed. Desuden ønskes muligheden for at kunne udvide vandværket på sigt og sikre fleksibilitet i forhold til den fremtidige efterspørgsel på rent vand. Det nye vandværk ved Løvbakkerne omfatter blandt andet byggemodning, vandværksbygning, el- og maskinan-læg, håndtering af skyllevand og overfladevand, vejanlæg og udenomsarealer på vandværksgrundens matrikel. Visionen hos ordregiver er, at vandværket opføres på en måde, hvor det integreres harmonisk og naturligt i land-skabet. Samtidig ønskes placeringen tæt på forsyningens boringer og eksisterende læringsmiljøer udnyttet, så vandværkets udearealer bliver centrum for et nyt læringsrum med fokus på bæredygtig vandforvaltning, grund-vandsbeskyttelse og formidling om vand. Det nye vandværk forventes færdigt medio 2029.

title: Contrôle Montage FO 2027-2028 - lignes aériennes et pylônes
description:
Le présent appel d’offres porte sur la réalisation de contrôles de montage dans le cadre du remplacement de câbles de garde existants par des câbles OPGW 144 FO sur différentes lignes aériennes à haute tension de Swissgrid.


Le marché est divisé en deux lots :


  • Lot 1 – Suisse alémanique,Tessin : contrôles de montage dans le cadre des projets TR1011, TR1270 et TR1930, représentant au total 361 pylônes et environ 125 km de lignes.
  • Lot 2 – Suisse romande : contrôles de montage dans le cadre des projets TR1570, TR1600 et TR1602, représentant au total 319 pylônes et environ 104 km de lignes.


Les prestations comprennent notamment le contrôle des fixations des câbles de garde, des ponts et des descentes des câbles de garde, des amortisseurs de vibrations et des balises, ainsi que le contrôle de la flèche des câbles de garde. Selon le projet, elles comprennent également le contrôle des systèmes Latchway, des dispositifs ou boulons d’ascension ainsi que d’autres adaptations réalisées sur les installations des lignes aériennes. Les contrôles de montage effectués doivent être documentés conformément aux procès-verbaux de contrôle prescrits.


L’étendue détaillée des prestations ainsi que les exigences et quantités spécifiques à chaque projet sont définies dans les documents d’appel d’offres.

title: Strømavtale for innkjøp og videreformidling av kraft
description: 1 Oppdraget 1.1 Om oppdragsgiveren Ål Kraftverk KF, heretter kalt oppdragsgiveren, innbyr til konkurranse om innkjøp av tjenester om innkjøp og formidling av kraft til Ål Kraftverk KFs kunder. Ål Kraftverk KF er et heleid kommunalt foretak som er eid av Ål kommune. Foretaket ble opprettet i 1914 og forvalter de kommunale kraftrettighetene for Ål kommune og drifter Ylifossen kraftverk. De kommunale kraftrettighetene består av ca. 101 GWh konsesjonskraft, 80 GWh Erstatningskraft og andelskraft fra Usta og Nest Kraftverk på 45-65 GWh. Kraftverket har også produksjon fra Ylifossen kraftverk på ca. 12 GWh og andel i Lya kravferk på 30 prosent som utgjør ca. 5. GWh. Kommunen får finansielt oppgjør per kvartal av inntekter og kostander fra Lya fra Hafslund Eco. Til sammen utgjør dette rettigheter og produksjon for kommunen på ca. 250 GWh. Foretaket har konsesjon for salg innen Ål kommune sine grenser og kjøper tjenester for om lag 3500 kunder. Foretakets kunder hadde behov for ca. 81,3 GWh i 2025. 1.2 Omfanget av oppdraget Denne anskaffelsen innebærer en avtale om en tjeneste i form av innkjøp og videreformidling av kraft til Ål kraftverk KFs sluttbrukerkunder. Foretaket tilbyr en rekke ulike produkter til næringskunder, innbyggere, fritidsboliger og til kommunalt forbruk. Tjenesten leverandøren skal utføre for Ål Kraftverk KF er å kjøpe inn kraft for å dekke behovet til Ål kraftverk KFs sluttbrukerkunder for de ulike produktene kraftverket tilbyr. Kommunen vil dekke avviket mellom tilbyderens utgifter til kjøp av kraft i spotmarkedet på NordPool og inntektene fra detaljsalg til kunder av Ål Kraftverk KF. Kommunen betaler – for sitt forbruk – i dag en fastpris for kraft på 15 øre/KWh, men dette er foreslått endret til 20 øre/KWh for å gjenspeile selvkosten for kraften. For de øvrige kunder tilbys følgende produkter: Spotpris Fleksikraft på 1. 2. eller 3 år . - Inntil 80 % av fjorårets forbruk til fastpris og forbruket over dette tilbys til spotpris uten påslag. Fastprisen varierer for hvor mange år kunden ønsker å binde seg. Fleksikraft tilbys alle kunder av Ål Kraftverk KF. 3. Ål Kraftverk – Vinter - Inntil 80 % av forventa årsforbruk med fast profil gjennom året. Avtalen gjelder fra 1. november til 30. april. For neste periode er prisen på 161,2 øre/KWh. For forbruket utover fastprisen gjelder spotpris uten påslag. 4. Ål Kraftverk KF har også en kundegruppe som mottar gratis kraft. Dette som en del av konsesjonsvilkår for Holsutbyggingen og kalles Votnakraft. Dette forbruket er på ca. 4,4 GWh og det er tale om ca. 250 anlegg. Se nærmere om kravene til leveransen som skal tilbys Ål Kraftverk KFs kunder under punkt 2. Kontraktene reguleres av kontraktsvilkårene som er vedlagt konkurransegrunnlaget og spesifikasjonene som kommer frem i konkurransegrunnlaget. 1.3 Anbudskonkurransen vektlegger ikke klima- og miljøhensyn Etter anskaffelsesloven § 5b fremgår det i annet ledd at en «oppdragsgiver skal vekte klima- og miljøhensyn med minimum tretti prosent». Det vil i denne anbudskonkurransen likevel ikke legges vekt på klima- og miljøhensyn da anskaffelsen har et «uvesentlig klimaavtrykk», jf. anskaffelsesloven § 5b tredje ledd. Tjenesten Ål Kraftverk KF anskaffer omhandler håndteringen av kjøp av kraft og videreformidling av Ål Kraftverks sluttbrukerkunder. Det er tale om menneskelige ressurser i form av arbeidsinnsats som kjøpes, der klimaavtrykket og miljøbelastningen ligger utenfor hva som kan knyttes til anskaffelsens art jf. Direktoratet for forvaltning og økonomistyring (DFØ) sin veileder om klima og miljøhensyn i offentlige anskaffelser. Kommunen er dermed unntatt forpliktelsene om å evaluere på klima og miljø. NB! Se vedlagte konkurransegrunnlag

buyer: Junta de Gobierno Local del Ayuntamiento de Alcalá de Guadaíra
title: Spain – Hotel accommodation services – concesión del servicio de explotación del Hotel Oromana (C-2026/032)
description: El objeto del presente contrato es la concesión del servicio de explotación del Hotel Oromana, de titularidad municipal, situado en el municipio de Alcalá de Guadaíra, que comprende la gestión integral del establecimiento, así como la ejecución de las actuaciones necesarias de rehabilitación, reforma, posible ampliación y adecuación del inmueble para su correcto funcionamiento y mejora de categoría, todo ello conforme a lo establecido en el correspondiente pliego de prescripciones técnicas. La presente contratación tiene como finalidad la transformación integral del establecimiento hotelero, con el objetivo de su adecuación a los estándares actuales del sector y su posicionamiento como hotel de cuatro estrellas, mediante la ejecución de las actuaciones constructivas necesarias y la implantación de un modelo de gestión profesionalizado, eficiente y orientado a la calidad. No se pretende con esta licitación una mera explotación del establecimiento en su estado actual, sino la definición y desarrollo de un proyecto global y coherente que integre la intervención sobre el inmueble con un modelo de gestión hotelera alineado con el valor patrimonial, paisajístico y turístico del entorno en el que se inserta, contribuyendo a reforzar la identidad y singularidad del destino. En este sentido, la concesión deberá orientarse a la creación de una oferta hotelera de calidad, capaz de atraer tanto a visitantes como a usuarios locales, generando actividad económica, empleo y sinergias con otros sectores vinculados al turismo, la cultura y la hostelería, y actuando como elemento dinamizador del municipio y su entorno. Asimismo, el contrato comprende tanto la ejecución de las obras definidas como obligatorias, como, en su caso, la incorporación de mejoras propuestas por los licitadores, así como la gestión integral del establecimiento, incluyendo todos los servicios necesarios para su correcto funcionamiento. El detalle y alcance de todas estas prestaciones se desarrollan en el pliego de prescripciones técnicas que rige la presente contratación.

title: Germany – Load-bearing structure design services – Ingenieurleistungen nach Teil 4 Abschnitt 1 HOAI (Tragwerksplanung)
description: Technische Hochschule Mannheim, 68163 Mannheim, Paul-Wittsack-Str. 6, Gebäude G (alt), Gesamtsanierung Laborgebäude Ingenieurleistungen der Tragwerksplanung nach Teil 4 Abschnitt 1 HOAI, Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 1 bis 6 sowie Besondere Leistungen der Leistungsphasen 1, 3, 4 und 8. Das Land Baden-Württemberg, vertreten durch Vermögen und Bau Baden-Württemberg, beabsichtigt die Generalsanierung des Gebäudes G (Altbau) der Technischen Hochschule Mannheim. Das Gebäude G (Altbau) der Technischen Hochschule Mannheim wurde in den Jahren 1970 bis 1972 errichtet und dient als Labor- und Hörsaalgebäude. Aufgrund der langen Nutzungszeit von über 50 Jahren entspricht das Gebäude in baulicher, brandschutztechnischer und haustechnischer Hinsicht nicht mehr dem heutigen Stand der Technik, daher soll es generalsaniert werden. Es handelt sich um einen zweigeschossigen Stahlbetonskelettbau mit Untergeschoss und einer Nutzfläche von 1.473 m². Es beinhaltet bisher auf beiden Geschossen Laborbereiche (Kategorie S1) mit einer großen Anzahl von Digestorien und einen sich über das UG und EG erstreckenden innenliegenden Hörsaal mit ansteigendem Gestühl, im Bestand derzeit ohne natürliche Belichtung. Das Gebäude hat eine Grundfläche von 26,10m x 39,90m. Die Flächen der Generalsanierung belaufen sich auf 1.473 m² NUF R, die Gesamtfläche mit Verkehrs- und Technikflächen beläuft sich auf 2.929 m² NRF. Die Nutzung als Labor- und Hörsaalgebäude bleibt auch für die Zukunft erhalten. Die Generalsanierung beinhaltet den Rückbau des Gebäudes bis auf die statische Konstruktion. Die bisherige Stahlbetonfertigteilfassade wird demontiert - hier ist in gestalterischer und energetischer Hinsicht eine komplett neue Fassade gewünscht. Moderne Lernformen sind bei der Neukonzeption zu berücksichtigen und zu ermöglichen, etwa Lernflächen in den Flurzonen oder Projektgruppen-Arbeitsräume. Bisher fehlende Funktionsräume wie z. B. Umkleiden für die Labore oder barrierefreie WC-Anlagen sind zu ergänzen. Die geschätzten Bauwerkskosten sind ca. 19,3 Mio. €, für die KG 300 wird von 8,1 Mio. € und für die KG 400 von 11,2 Mio. € ausgegangen. Die bauzeitliche, geprüfte Statik von 1969 inkl. Nachträgen liegt vor, eine repräsentative Bestandsaufnahme und Bewertung tragender Bauteile ist dennoch notwendig. Der Baubeginn ist für Ende 2030 geplant, die Baufertigstellung für Ende 2033.

Die aktuelle Versorgungsstruktur der JVA Fuhlsbüttel sowie die Wegeführungen auf dem Anstaltsgelände sind aufgrund des Freizugs der Teilfläche anzupassen. Zur Abgrenzung der verbleibenden Anstaltsfläche gegenüber der freizuziehenden Teilfläche ist außerdem die Außensicherung der JVA Fuhlsbüttel in Teilen neu zu planen und zu versetzen. Hierfür sind einige Bestandsbauten der Anstalt vollständig oder in Teilen zurückzubauen Am Standort der JVA Fuhlsbüttel sollen zwei Ersatzneubauten erstellt werden; ein Ausbildungsgebäude (A), dieses zentral auf dem JVA-Gelände, sowie ein Garagen- und Verwaltungsgebäude (B) mit Anbindung an eine Bestandspforte. Die jeweils viergeschossigen Neubauten werden als Mischkonstruktion aus Mauerwerk, Ortbeton und Betonfertigteilelementen, ohne Unterkellerung mit einer Sohle aus WU-Beton erstellt. Die Außenhüllen der Gebäude werden mit Verblendsteinen bekleidet und erhalten ein Satteldach als Pfettendach aus Nadelholz mit Metalldacheindeckung. Sämtliche Fensteröffnungen werden vergittert, Hauptgegenstand der Ausschreibung sind die Lieferung und Montage von Innentüren aus Holz- und Holzwerkstoffen einschl. Stahlzargen. _________________________________________________________________________ Wesentliche Arbeiten: Für die Neubauten ATV DIN 18355 Tischlerarbeiten

title: Germany – Contractor's all-risk insurance services – BauRisk-Versicherung
description: degewo AG ist mit 82.000 eigen- und fremdverwalteten Wohnungen eines der größten kommunalen Wohnungsunternehmen in Deutschland mit Sitz in Berlin. Die Immobilienbestände befinden sich in allen Stadtteilen Berlins und vergrößern sich im Zuge von Investitionsmaßnahmen stetig. Die netzWerk ist als 100%ige Tochtergesellschaft der degewo im Bereich Energieversorgung und technische Gebäudeinfrastruktur als konzernangehöriges Dienstleistungsunternehmen tätig. Der netzWerk obliegt dabei unter anderem die effiziente, klimaschonende und intelligente Versorgung des Konzerngebäudebestandes mit Wärme und Strom. Gegenstand ist eine kombinierte Bauleistungs- und Haftpflicht-Versicherung (BauRisk-Versicherung) mit den Vertragsteilen Bauleistungs-, Betriebshaftpflicht- (einschließlich Bauherren-, Umwelthaftpflicht- und Umweltschaden-) und Berufshaftpflicht-Versicherung für alle Bau- und Montageprojekte (Strom-/Wärmeerzeugungsanlagen und Strom-/Wärmeversorgungsanlagen einschließlich Photovoltaikanlagen sowie Kabel- und Glasfasernetze) der Versicherungsnehmerin mit einer Gesamt-Bausumme von über 200.000 € bis 25.000.000 € und einem Planungsbeginn ab 2027 einschließlich der dazugehörigen Tiefbaumaßnahmen mit einer jeweiligen vorläufigen Gesamtbausumme über 200.000 € und bis 25.000.000 € innerhalb der Bundesrepublik Deutschland, die von der Versicherungsnehmerin oder den versicherten Unternehmen (gem. Ziffer 2a) beauftragt und während der Vertragslaufzeit begonnen werden. Sämtliche am Bau beteiligten Firmen der Bereiche Ausführung und Planung sollen im Rahmen dieser kombinierten Bauleistungs-, Montage- und Haftpflicht-Versicherung abgesichert werden und müssen insofern keine eigene Versicherung mehr vorhalten. Als Versicherungsort gelten für jedes Bauprojekt das gesamte Baustellengelände inkl. für das Projekt genutzte Lagergelegenheiten bzw. Verbindungswege zwischen den vorgenannten Orten innerhalb der Bundesrepublik Deutschland. Im Ergebnis des Vergabeverfahrens kann ein Versichererkonsortium nach den zum Gegenstand dieses Verfahrens gemachten Vergabeunterlagen gebildet werden. Für ein Führungsangebot wird eine Zeichnungsquote von mindestens 40 % vorausgesetzt werden, für ein Beteiligungsangebot eine Zeichnungsquote von mindestens 20 %. Die Bewerber erklären mit der Angebotsabgabe die grundsätzliche Bereitschaft, mit den von der Auftraggeberin ausgewählten Mitgliedern des Versichererkonsortiums zusammenzuarbeiten.

buyer: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control
title: Sweden – Health services – SPR/260834 - Provision of genomic epidemiology and public health bioinformatics training
description: The overall objective of this tender is to procure a Framework Contract to strengthen the capacity for genomic epidemiology and public health bioinformatics through interdisciplinary trainings, which is crucial for response during a pandemic or unexpected major public health events. The general objectives of the trainings are to support countries in building up their capacity in genomic epidemiology and bioinformatics for public health purposes, and to increase the interdisciplinary collaboration between bioinformaticians, epidemiologists and microbiologists within a country to facilitate the routine use of genomic information for surveillance, preparedness, and outbreak response. Activities shall also enhance data sharing and collaborations between public health institutions and ECDC, and enhanced networking activities will foster cross-border collaborations. The target groups for the trainings are professionals working in public health institutions with a background in computational biology and bioinformatics; and professionals working in public health institutions who do not have a specific background in bioinformatics. The aims of the trainings are: * To allow the professionals with a background in computational biology and bioinformatics to: - enhance and extend their skills in order to strengthen their capacity in the field of public health bioinformatics; - better understand the needs and concepts of epidemiology and public health microbiology, with a focus on the inputs and outputs needed by their counterparts (i.e. microbiologists, epidemiologists, professionals in public health surveillance and response) to take rapid and informed public health action. * To allow the professionals without a background in computational biology/bioinformatics to: - gain a better understanding of how genomic epidemiology can be applied in a public health context with special focus on how traditional and genomic data can be jointly analysed, interpreted and used for public health purposes; - become more familiar with the concepts, formats and conventions commonly used in microbial genomics, and get a better understanding of how the structure and format of the data can be used to streamline the data analysis process; - better understand the concepts behind and use of the most common bioinformatic tools and pipelines used for epidemiological analyses, including limitations and possible alternatives; and - gain a better overview of the basic principles, options for and best practices of data storage, management and sharing, with a specific focus on sequencing data and associated metadata.

title: Germany – Architectural services for outdoor areas – Neubau Bildungscampus Eslohe - Objektplanung Freianlagen
description: Am Bildungsstandort Eslohe befindet sich das zentrale Kompetenzzentrum des Dachdeckerhandwerks in Westfalen. Der Standort vereint die schulische Berufsausbildung, die Unterbringung der Auszubildenden, Verpflegungsangebote sowie Maßnahmen der Aus- und Weiterbildung in einem zusammenhängenden Campus. Die bestehende Gebäudeinfrastruktur stammt überwiegend aus den Jahren 1968 und 1985. Die vorhandenen Gebäude entsprechen sowohl hinsichtlich ihrer funktionalen Struktur als auch in Bezug auf die bauliche, energetische und nutzungsspezifische Qualität nicht mehr den heutigen Anforderungen an einen modernen Bildungs- und Internatsstandort. Insbesondere die bestehende Mischnutzung von Unterricht, Verwaltung, Wohnen und Verpflegung innerhalb der vorhandenen Gebäude führt zu organisatorischen Einschränkungen und erschwert eine zeitgemäße Umsetzung des Bildungsauftrags. Auch die Unterbringungssituation im Wohnheimbereich entspricht nicht mehr den aktuellen Anforderungen. Die derzeit überwiegend vorhandenen Mehrbettzimmer mit Gemeinschaftssanitäranlagen bieten nur eingeschränkte Aufenthalts- und Wohnqualität. Darüber hinaus bestehen Defizite bei den Freizeit-, Aufenthalts- und Kommunikationsflächen für die Auszubildenden. Im Rahmen einer Machbarkeitsstudie wurden verschiedene Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten für den Standort untersucht. Auf Grundlage der Ergebnisse hat sich der Auftraggeber für die Realisierung eines Ersatzneubaukonzeptes entschieden. Damit sollen die funktionalen, organisatorischen, pädagogischen und energetischen Anforderungen langfristig erfüllt und gleichzeitig der laufende Schul- und Wohnheimbetrieb während der Realisierung sichergestellt werden.

Sowohl die Raumwirkung als auch die angestrebte Nutzung des Kraftwerkgebäudes ist für das angrenzende Blumenthal-Gelände von Bedeutung und wirkt sich auf die Zukunftsperspektive der Flächenentwicklung von "Blumenthal hoch3" erheblich aus. Das wichtigste Kriterium, die dauerhafte Aufrechterhaltung der Zufahrt zur Nephrologie in Haus B, ist über die gesamte Bauzeit zwingend zu gewährleisten. Die Ausführung hat daher in mindestens zwei separaten, zeitlich versetzten Bauabschnitten (jeweils halbseitige Sperrung der Zufahrtsstraße) zu erfolgen. Die vollständige Erreichbarkeit von Haus B (Nephrologie) für Rettungsfahrzeuge und Dialysepatienten ist rund um die Uhr (24/7) sicherzustellen. Alle Kosten für mehrfache Anfahrten, das abschnittsweise Umsetzen von Maschinen sowie für Vorhaltungen sind in die Pauschale einzukalkulieren. Für die im Baufeld befindlichen Bestandsbäume wurde bereits eine Fällgenehmigung eingereicht. Sollte die Asphaltdeckschicht aufgrund der Witterungsverhältnisse erst verspätet ausgeführt werden können, ist dies zulässig. Der betroffene Bereich darf jedoch auch abschnittsweise nicht länger als 7 Wochen gesperrt werden. Daher muss zumindest die Asphalttragschicht eingebaut werden, bevor es zu einer längeren Unterbrechung kommt bzw. um sicherzustellen, dass der Parkplatz nicht länger als 7 Wochen gesperrt bleibt.

buyer: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
title: Germany – Vocational training services – 10018858-Implementation of TVET support and women's economic empowerment activities in Sierra Leone
description: Sierra Leone faces persistent poverty, high informality and limited job creation, disproportionately affecting women and youth. Agriculture is the largest employer, yet value chains are fragmented, processing is weak, and access to finance, quality infrastructure and certification is limited. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system suffers from outdated curricula, insufficient equipment and low private sector engagement, constraining labour market relevance, especially for women and returnees. The "Youth Employment Promotion through Socio Ecological and Economic Transformation of selected rural Value Chains" (EET project), commissioned by BMZ with EU co funding, supports inclusive, market oriented growth and better employment along selected value chains (cassava, coffee/cocoa, vegetables, poultry). It strengthens micro, small and medium sized enterprises (MSMEs) and the enabling ecosystem, with a strong focus on Women's Economic Empowerment (WEE) and youth integration. The project applies a concise multi level approach: support MSMEs with training, coaching and finance to improve productivity and market access; strengthen ecosystem actors (finance, certification, cooperatives, processing centres) to enhance services and linkages; and upgrade TVET through demand driven Competence Based Education and Training (CBET) curricula, improved facilities at Government Technical Institutes (GTIs) in Kabala, Kailahun, Koidu and Mattru Jong, teacher capacity building and institutionalised private sector engagement for apprenticeships and certification via Industry Sector Advisory Committees. WEE is embedded throughout. The project strengthens six representative bodies advancing women's economic rights (e.g. Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment - GEWE - Act), introduces gender transformative modules (Gender makes Business Sense - GmBS; Gender Action Learning Systems - GALS; Gender Model Family - GMF) via public and private providers, and delivers mentoring and awareness campaigns to address norms and improve women"s access to resources, markets and decision making. Outcomes are tracked with recognised tools such as the (pro )Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (pro WEAI). Key results targeted include: - Improved competitiveness of MSMEs with measurable employment effects for women and youth. - Upgraded GTIs and at least nine demand oriented, gender responsive curricula operational; teachers trained in learner centred CBET; trainees certified in line with National Council for Technical and Vocational Education (NCTVE) standards in the initial phase. - Stronger institutional conditions for women's economic participation, including operational representative bodies, integrated gender transformative modules, and functioning mentoring and communication platforms. - Enhanced market access through strengthened outgrower networks, cooperative services and business linkages, enabling more equitable participation of women and young producers. The approach is rights based, conflict and context sensitive, and climate aware. It promotes green and circular economy elements in training and enterprise support, limits environmental footprints and applies Do No Harm principles. Implementation aligns with national policies (TVET Policy, Dual Apprenticeship Policy) under the coordination of the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development, with the Ministry of Technical and Higher Education (MTHE) and NCTVE responsible for TVET standards and certification, and the Ministry of Gender and Children's Affairs and civil society partners advancing WEE. Continuous monitoring, learning and adaptive management ensure data driven steering and accountability to BMZ and the EU. EU visibility will follow EU visual identity guidelines; co branding with BMZ/GIZ will follow donor rules.?

description: The GIZ programme "UfM Hub for Jobs, Trade and Investment II", commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and co-financed by the European Union, strengthens regional economic cooperation and policy dialogue across the Mediterranean, reinforcing the Union for the Mediterranean (UfM) as the principal regional platform for cooperation between European and Southern Mediterranean partner countries. The programme contributes to the implementation of the EU Pact for the Mediterranean and supports the regional Team Europe Initiative (TEI) "Jobs through Trade & Investment in the Southern Neighbourhood", promoting structured exchange among governments, regional organisations, the private sector, financial institutions and other stakeholders. While the programme focuses on UfM Member States in North Africa and the Middle East, EU Member States and the Western Balkans are actively involved in peer learning and the exchange of best practices. A further priority is strengthening the institutional capacities of the UfM Secretariat to enhance its role in facilitating regional cooperation. Within this framework, the programme also implements the regional Action "Digital Transformation in the Southern Neighbourhood" (DTSN), which covers the thematic areas Digital and Telecommunications Regulation, Cybersecurity (implemented by the GIZ Global Program "Partnerships for Cybersecurity"), and Digital Skills. DTSN supports countries in advancing regulatory approximation with EU best practice, strengthening national regulatory authorities (NRAs), institutionalising the Euro-Mediterranean Regulators Group (EMERG), improving national cybersecurity governance, and developing regional digital skills systems geared to the needs of MSMEs and business support organisations.

description: The objective of GIZ's global project Sustainable Economic Transformation and Sustainable Finance is to advance the transformation towards a more sustainable economy and financial sector, grounded in international standards and global agendas. To this end, the project implements activities in three main areas of intervention: - Pillar 1: Fostering global knowledge exchange and peer-learning regarding the sustainable transformation of the economy and the financial sector. - Pillar 2: Supporting development of policy and regulatory frameworks in partner countries governing the transformation toward a sustainable economy and financial sector in partner countries. - Pillar 3: Providing advisory services and technical assistance to embed sustainability in governance and financial decision-making of financial institutions. In pillar 2, the project supports partner countries in aligning their financial regulatory and policy frameworks with international standards and best practices on sustainable finance. This encompasses, for example, the development of taxonomies, disclosure regulations, sustainable financial product standards or policies on ESG risk management. The project's activities include, for example, supporting the development of national taxonomies in Rwanda, Peru, Senegal, Ghana, The Philippines, and Mexico. The support provided by GIZ is comprehensive, including strategic advice, capacity building, design of multi-stakeholder processes (e.g., coordination of technical expert groups, support for public consultation), drafting advice (e.g., on the selection of sectors and screening criteria), and supporting the taxonomy's dissemination and implementation. This process is complemented by peer-learning opportunities and featuring lessons learned from implementation in partner countries in relevant international and regional forums. The objective of this tender is to establish a flexible pool of specialized technical expertise that can support sustainable finance taxonomy initiatives in partner countries designated by GIZ during the contract period. The contractor will provide advisory services covering the development, enhancement and implementation of sustainable finance taxonomies, as well as related analytical work, capacity building and knowledge products.

title: Nose Plug and Support Cup
description: *The purpose of this amendment 2 to Sources Sought is to notify contractors of the following below: PIEE Solicitation Module Notification The Government intends to utilize the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module for the posting, dissemination, and receipt of proposals for any subsequent solicitation resulting from this market research. To ensure your organization is prepared to access solicitation documents and submit responses, interested offerors are encouraged to review the PIEE Solicitation Module registration instructions provided as an attachment to this posting. Offerors are advised to complete the registration process prior to any potential solicitation release to avoid delays. Please see the links to self-guided help for registration and training in the PIEE Solicitation Module below: https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/cap/docs/piee/PIEE_Solicitation_Module_Vendor_Access_Instructions.pdf https://pieetraining.eb.mil/wbt/xhtml/wbt/sol/index.xhtml This amendment 2 is not to reopen the Sources Sought for submissions as it has already been closed as of 02 September, 2025. **The purpose of this amendment 1 to Sources Sought is to revise the response date from 02 Sept 2025 to 22 Sept 2025. The Army Contracting Command - Rock Island, on behalf of the Project Manager Closed Combat Systems, Picatinny Arsenal, NJ, is issuing a sources sought notice to identify capable sources for the production and delivery of the following items. Item NSN: Part Number Nose Plug (G008) 1325-00-124-1538 9211803 Support Cup (FW26) 1325-00-609-2344 1211676 ITEM DESCRIPTIONS: The following parts are used on various MK80 General Purpose bombs. Nose Plug (G008): The nose closing plug is a forged solid piece of metal (cone shaped) with a 3.5-inch threaded area. It has two cutout areas in the cone which are used for wrenching purposes. Primary use of metal nose closing plug (when used with nose support cup) is to prevent fuze-well collapse on impact when nose fuzing is not utilized. If nose fuze well were to collapse on impact, a low order detonation may occur. In addition, metal nose closing plugs may be used in cement-filled bombs to prevent cement particles from being ingested into aircraft engines. The Government anticipates a maximum quantity of 20,000-30,000 per year. CRITICAL PROCESSES/SKILLS: The manufacture of this item requires skills, which include, but are not limited to: Forging and Heat-Treating Equipment, Machining Equipment (Lathe) Support Cup (FW26): The support cup is used in the nose cavity to prevent collapse of the fuze cavity on heavy impact when the bomb is tail fuzed only. The metal nose support cup is a piece of 2.87-inch tubing wedged on one end to form a beveled area. There is a 1.62-inch hole beveled end to allow the support cup to slip over fuze well nut. The Government anticipates a maximum quantity of 20,000-30,000 per year. CRITICAL PROCESSES/SKILLS: The manufacture of this item requires skills, which include, but are not limited to: Cleaning and Coating, Machining equipment (Lathe) An acceptable vendor must be able to display the skills of its employees and established expertise in completing essential operations of manufacturing the Nose Plug and Support Cup. Respondents to this Sources Sought must have or have the ability to obtain the available skills required to perform all production and testing operations necessary to deliver conforming end items to the Government. These skills must be available with sufficient experience and proficiency to produce these items in a timely and efficient manner. A respondent must also have or have the ability to obtain the appropriate machinery, tooling, and manufacturing engineering skills required to support quality production limitations. Any significant lead times with equipment or materials associated with production of these items should also be noted. RESPONSES: Interested companies who consider themselves capable of manufacturing the Nose Plug and Support Cup, are invited to indicate their interest by providing the Government with the following information: a.) A brief summary of the company�s capabilities (a description of the facilities, personnel experience, quality system, and past manufacturing experience) and capacity. If a respondent does not have adequate resources (facilities, technical, manufacturing, personnel, etc.) available, then it must be able to demonstrate its ability to obtain those resources without significant delay. b.) Identify and include a brief summary of any potential key sub-tier vendors or subcontractors and identify key components or processes that would be subcontracted. c.) Provide a rough order of magnitude (ROM) prices for an approximate yearly FY27-31 production quantity of 20,000 � 30,000 quantities for each part. d.) Identify minimum and maximum monthly production quantities and identify the available capacity considering any other known production. e.) Identify your company�s size status for the identified NAICS code in the response. f.) Due to the current global supply chain and other factors, respondents are asked to identify any components or materials that may be subject to price volatility or scarcity and address what their firm is doing to mitigate risk related to obtaining materials, price impacts, and production stability. Technical Data Packages: The Technical Data Packages (TDPs) associated with this requirement are classified as Distribution D � limited distribution authorized to the Department of Defense (DoD) and U.S. DoD Contractors Only. These documents contain technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act (Title 22, U.S.C., SEC 2751, ET SEQ.) or the Export Administration Act of 1979 (Title 50, U.S.C., APP 2401 et seq.), as Amended. Violations of these export laws are subject to severe criminal penalties. Disseminate in accordance with provisions of DoD Directive 5230.25. Interested vendors must be registered with the U.S./Canada Joint Certification Program (JCP) to gain access to the TDPs (see www.dlis.dla.mil/jcp/ for instruction and information). Each individual requiring access to the TDPs must have a SAM.gov account prior to accessing the TDPs. Access to the TDP will only be granted to those individuals who are listed as the Data Custodian (block 3) on the DD Form 2345, Military Critical Technical Data Requirement, which was required to be registered within the JCP. The Data Custodian is the sole representative identified to receive export controlled TDPs and drawings. To obtain the top-level drawings, interested vendors with the proper certification in JCP, may request explicit access through the �attachments/links� tab in SAM.gov under this posting. In addition to making the request by the JCP Data Custodian in SAM.gov, interested vendors should also send a copy of their approved DD2345 to the points of contact specified below. For the purpose of this Sources Sought, a top-level drawing will be provided for the Nose Plug and Support Cup. The NAICS code for these items is 332993 with a business size standard of 1,500 employees. As noted above, please indicate your business size and socio-economic status in your response. Also be sure to provide the company name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, taxpayer identification number, DUNS number, and CAGE Code. title: PBA Testing, Lab and Engineering Services
description: This procurement is in support of Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA). PBA performs a variety of missions for the Department of Defense, including the manufacture and demilitarization of ammunition and related components. To accomplish this mission within the environmental protections established by the Clean Air Act (CAA), Clean Water Act (CWA), Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), the Comprehensive Environmental Restoration and Compensation Liability Act (CERCLA), and the Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) regulations. In addition to the aforementioned regulations, to accomplish the mission, PBA must comply within requirements established by the Defense Environmental Restoration Program (DERP). PBA is seeking contract services related to these requirements. This effort will augment on-going on-site laboratory evaluations in several media.

Solid waste may include used mattresses, broken furniture, used carpeting, bundled cardboard, construction rubble, etc. Solid waste will not include any items considered hazardous waste, medical waste, or waste defined by the EPA as being not general solid waste. Contractor Compliance: Contractor shall assume full responsibility for compliance with all current Federal, State, City, and County laws, VHA M-1 Part VII Chapter 14 dated 9/19/94, rules and regulations governing the collection, removal, and disposal of solid waste. Contractor shall be responsible for providing copies of all necessary permits/documents upon VA request. Contractor shall dispose of solid waste collected from the VA in such a manner as not to cause conditions detrimental to public health or to constitute a public nuisance. Contractor shall assume full responsibility for clean up in the event solid waste is released into the environment accidentally or otherwise, on or off VA property because of the Contractor s actions. Schedule Work: Contractor shall provide a schedule of services agreeable to both the Contractor and VA. This schedule will be determined by the size and types of collection containers utilized and the types of containers that food waste will be collected in. Contractor shall provide service on regular business days, Monday through Friday, between the hours of 7:00am and 4:30pm. In the event a scheduled pick-up falls on a federal holiday the pick-up will take place no later than the next business day. Unscheduled Work: From time to time there may be special needs that require immediate attention by the Contract at contractor expense, such as, a collection container or compactor repair (Non-VA Owned) or collection container was missed on a regularly scheduled pick-up. When this occurs the Contracting Officers Representative (COR) will place a call notifying Contractor of the situation. The Contractor shall respond the next business day during the hours of operation from 7:00am to 4:30pm to resolve the issue, even if that falls on a weekend or holiday, unless otherwise agreed upon by the COR. In the event inclement weather causes a delay in service the Contractor shall provide service no later than the next business day. Availability of Utilities: The VA shall furnish at no expense to the Contractor, electricity at existing outlets for Contractor s use in performing this contract. Should the Contractor propose a plan that is beneficial to the VA in which additional electrical outlets would be required, the VA may consider installing them at the VA s expense. At no time will the Contractor make any modifications to the electrical outlets without prior approval by the VA. Vehicles: The Contractor shall use vehicles specifically designed for waste collection that have watertight bodies and do not permit loss of waste. Open box trucks, with canvas covers, shall not be permitted with the sole exception of specially requested roll off containers. Vehicles shall be maintained in good repair, operate safely, be relatively clean, and not be considered unsightly. Vehicles considered by the COR not to meet the prior minimum standards will not be permitted to collect waste on VA property until corrected. The Contractor shall have sufficient vehicles for backup of regularly assigned vehicles to insure completion of contract requirements in the event of breakdowns or other unforeseen problems. Containers: Contractor shall provide easy loadable, leak proof, industrial heavy- duty type solid waste containers that have working lids/covers. Containers that are mounted on wheels shall have a mechanism that locks the wheels for safety. Containers shall be maintained in good operating condition, cleaned regularly, and shall not be unsightly. No containers or lids shall be rusty, bent, or damaged. Containers identified by the VA that do not meet these standards shall be replaced or repaired within seven (7) calendar days unless otherwise agreed upon by the VA. All containers should be of sufficient size to hold a minimum of three to four days worth of solid waste. Compactor shall meet the standard safety guidelines to protect the operators from accidental injury or death. Compactor containers shall be operational year-round regardless of weather and temperatures. All equipment supplied must be fit for the duty to which it is intended. List of Current Containers: Hot Springs: 7 each - 4-yard containers (building 12) 3 each 1-yard containers (building 11) 1 each 6-yard compactor (building 12) 1 each 6-yard container for compactor (building 12) Fort Meade: 1 each 40-yard compactor (located at building 145 dock) 1 each 40-yard container for compactor (located at building 88) 3 each 30-yard containers (east yard behind boiler plant area) Additional Containers Upon Request: Hot Springs: 2 each 30-yard containers upon request annually (request may be two different dates for a maximum of 2 containers in total in a year time frame) Collection Areas: Contractor shall provide a sufficient number of containers of appropriate size to match the requirements of the BHHCS, additional containers shall be provided as deemed necessary. Contractor shall insure that the area immediately surrounding waste containers is clean. Any large solid waste that will not fit into a waste container will also be removed at the Contractor s earliest convenience; time will not exceed more than seven (7) days. Waste Weights: Contractor shall provide written verifiable actual weights of the solid waste collected and removed by the type of wastes, from the VA with each monthly billing cycle. In addition, if there is waste that the Contractor takes to a Recycling Facility the Contractor shall provide specific weights to the VA for tracking purposes. Examples of this would be cardboard, paper, bundles, metals and compost. title: GOCO Industry Day
description: Executive Summary The current operating strategy for Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) Army ammunition plants requires reassessment to ensure the Organic Industrial Base can meet future requirements for safety, responsiveness, capacity, modernization, supply-chain resilience, and affordable lifecycle performance. Traditional GOCO competition and contract approaches may not consistently create the incentives, flexibility, or accountability necessary to operate Government-owned facilities as modern and competitive manufacturing enterprises. In particular, existing approaches may overemphasize Government-directed workload and reimbursed facility operations rather than operator responsibility for productive utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce development, workload capture, and operational performance. The Government is seeking industry input on a commercially disciplined GOCO operating model that preserves Government mission priorities while providing the operating contractor meaningful responsibility and flexibility to manage the facility as a competitive manufacturing enterprise. Under such a model, the contractor would be expected to sustain, modernize, maintain, and improve the facility through efficient operations, productive utilization, pursuit of approved workload, and sound business practices. The Government seeks to identify contracting, workload, risk-allocation, facility-use, oversight, intellectual-property, and performance-management constructs that will enable this model while preserving appropriate Government accountability, safety, security, and access to required production capacity. Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE AS&A) is assessing the future GOCO operating strategy before proceeding with future GOCO competitions. Purpose Army Contracting Command � Rock Island, on behalf of PAE AS&A, intends to host an Industry Day in November 2026 focused on transforming the operating strategy for GOCO Army ammunition plants. Specific Industry Day details will be provided separately; registration is not currently required. This Request for Information (RFI), together with the subsequent Industry Day, will help the Government understand feasible business and operating models for future GOCO facilities. The Government will use industry feedback to inform discussion of alternative approaches to facility operations, modernization, workload management, contract structure, and oversight. Objective The Government�s objective is to establish a commercially disciplined operating model for GOCO Army ammunition plants that improves responsiveness to Warfighter requirements while sustaining long-term plant viability, modernization, competitiveness, and accountability. The desired model would provide the operating contractor with appropriate flexibility and meaningful responsibility to manage facility utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce, supply chain, and approved workload. The Government seeks input on the risk-allocation mechanisms, workload authorities, facility-use structures, performance measures, and oversight approaches necessary to support this model while preserving Government mission priorities. The desired end state is a modern, flexible production enterprise capable of efficiently increasing, reducing, pausing, restarting, changing over, and surging production in response to Warfighter need without disproportionate impacts to cost, schedule, quality, workforce readiness, safety, or production capability. The Government is particularly interested in performance measures that demonstrate: Safe and reliable operations; Schedule reliability and order-to-delivery responsiveness; Plant availability and production throughput; Rapid changeover, shutdown, restart, and surge capability; Flexible, modular, dual-use, and/or automated manufacturing capacity; Effective maintenance, workforce, and supply-chain management; Competitive lifecycle cost and productive utilization; Modernization outcomes that improve operating performance; and Appropriate transparency and accountability without unnecessary Government direction of day-to-day operations. Areas of Consideration The Government developed the attached questionnaire based on the following interconnected areas of consideration. Respondents are requested to complete the associated questionnaire and provide practical recommendations, examples, and lessons learned from relevant commercial, defense-industrial, or other manufacturing environments. The Government is particularly interested in responses that: Describe a complete and coherent commercial operating model rather than isolated contractual changes; Identify recommended Government and contractor responsibilities; Explain the proposed allocation of risk and opportunity; Identify measurable outcomes and recommended key performance indicators; Describe the conditions necessary to modernize facilities and maintain flexible production capacity; Address how the model would operate during high-demand, low-demand, shutdown, restart, and surge conditions; Identify legal, regulatory, technical, security, safety, qualification, or business constraints requiring further Government consideration; and Contain data that supports its recommended solutions. 1. Commercial Operating Model and Risk Allocation The Government seeks input on operating models in which the contractor manages a Government-owned facility with commercial discipline while meeting Government mission priorities. Topics may include: Operator responsibilities, decision rights, and accountability; Allocation of demand, utilization, revenue, operating-cost, maintenance, modernization, obsolescence, and performance risk; Contractor responsibility for productive utilization and continuous improvement; Mechanisms that encourage modernization as an operating outcome rather than a discrete facility-improvement project; Gain-sharing, profit-sharing, retained earnings, or reinvestment approaches; Treatment of contractor-funded improvements at contract transition; and Protection of Government interests while maintaining meaningful contractor performance and market risk. 2. Demand, Capacity, and Workload Management The Government seeks input on how Government requirements and approved non-Government workload can be integrated to improve plant utilization, responsiveness, and long-term viability. Topics may include: Government demand forecasting and demand-signal quality; Government mission-priority requirements; Capacity reservation, surge, turn-down, shutdown, restart, and reconstitution; Minimum Government commitments, if necessary, and the appropriate purpose and scope of such commitments; Integration of Government, commercial, Foreign Military Sales, and other approved workload; Multi-year procurement and workload-planning approaches; Workforce retention and readiness during periods of variable demand; and Mechanisms for balancing Government access to capacity with contractor responsibility for utilization. 3. Modern, Flexible, and Resilient Production The Government seeks concepts for modernizing GOCO production capability to improve agility, resilience, and efficient response to changing demand. Topics may include: Flexible, modular, dual-use, and automated production lines; Rapid product changeover and qualification; Planned shutdown, restart, and surge capability; Automation, robotics, digital manufacturing, digital twins, and predictive maintenance; Equipment replacement, facility renewal, and obsolescence management; Workforce cross-training and critical-skill retention; Supply-chain resilience and access to existing U.S. industrial capacity; and Technical, regulatory, contractual, qualification, or facility barriers that limit modernization and flexibility. 4.
