title: J065--635-27-1-455-0003 PM and Repair Services for Stryker Operon Surgical Tables Contract (VA-27-00001610)
description: BACKGROUND: Equipment: The following systems of equipment require service under this contract. This includes sub-systems, components, software, hardware, and parts. Equipment Description Brand & Model Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Serial Number VA PMI Number Tables: Operating Surgical Table, Operon D860 Stryker 03010474 81390 Tables: Operating Surgical Table, Operon D860 Stryker 02806707 81391 Tables: Operating Surgical Table, Operon D860 Stryker 02863505 81392 Tables: Operating Surgical Table, Operon D860 Stryker 02861070 81393 Tables: Operating Surgical Table, Operon D860 Stryker 02928652 81394 Tables: Operating Surgical Table, Operon D860 Stryker 02790672 81395 Tables: Operating Surgical Table, Operon D860 Stryker 02791371 81396 SUMMARY OF REQUIREMENTS Contractor shall provide OEM-trained technicians to perform OEM-standard services on equipment in this PWS. Services on the equipment include maintenance support, corrective maintenance repair, 24x7 emergency phone support, provision of parts (comprehensive parts coverage), and service and modification as required due to safety or reliability. All OEM software updates shall be included. Tasks and Requirements Performance and Repairs: All work performed shall be in accordance with manufacturer s specifications, including but not limited to adjustments, calibrating, cleaning, lubricating, testing, disassembly, checkout, replacement of parts, etc. required to keep the equipment in operating condition. Contractor must guarantee 95% up time for the equipment. Contractor shall guarantee that all equipment covered by this contract shall be in optimum working condition at the completion of each contracted Period of Performance. Contractor will make every attempt to maintain and repair equipment on-site within a reasonable time, unless local environment prohibits on-site attendance. Failing this, contractor will provide substitute equipment in the event a repair continues beyond the reasonable time frame. A reasonable time frame ensures the VA mission continues uninterrupted with no loss, damage or suffering to VA patients and resources. Preventive Maintenance: Contractor shall provide periodic preventive maintenance service on equipment within the interval(s) set by the OEM (ie, Annual, Semi-Annual, Quarterly), in scheduled month of each contracted Period of Performance, including all work between Standard Business Hours, weekend hours, and non-standard hours, and arranged through the COR. The contractor shall work with the COR, Surgery service and Sterile Processing Service to not disrupt patient care by scheduling PM visits in advance. The visits will include equipment verification by an OEM-trained technician. Before the expiration of each period of performance, the contractor shall provide the COR with a report certifying the equipment listed in this PWS has been calibrated to O.E.M. standards not less than OEM recommended interval(s) during the contract period. All parts shall be O.E.M. standard or certified. Service Call: Unscheduled service should be conducted at no additional cost during standard business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM 5:00 PM. Non-emergency service (machine still able to run with no increased patient risk) should be available, with a technician onsite at location, within 48 hours notice from the COR. If support call for repair service is deemed mission-critical, contractor will be on-site performing corrective action response to service calls within 24 hours of notice from COR, barring special circumstances. 24 hour service call center support should be available to schedule corrective service calls. Technical phone support shall be available weekdays from 7:00 AM 7:00 PM at no additional charge. Software Updates: Contractor shall provide any software updates, as they become available, for all equipment, at no additional cost. All software changes made become the property of the VA. Help Desk Support: Contractor shall provide emergency telephone support during Standard Business Hours, as a minimum at no additional charge, with phone calls returned no later than 2 hours after a voice message has been left by the COR. Modifications: If contractor or external hazard assessment/notification by the FDA, NCPS, or CEOSH determines that a modification is necessary to address safety concerns or reliability, installation and modification will be performed at no additional charge. Parts: As part of the OEM-standard of service required on this contract, contractor must provide unique and/or high mortality replacement parts. All parts will be O.E.M. recommended parts. Contractor must provide repair services on batteries and handpieces, at no additional cost to the government. This includes provision of replacement/loaner parts and shipment costs, such as loaner handpieces. To maintain continuity of patient care, contractor must ship replacement/loaner handpieces overnight to the VA within 48 hours of receipt of notice by the VA that a hand piece needs to be repaired due to normal wear and tear. Once the loaner is received by the VA, the VA will ship the government-owned hand piece to the contractor. If the government-owned hand piece is not able to be repaired the contractor must return the broken handpiece to the VA with written notification of what prevented the repair and the issues causing the part not to function the way the OEM intended. If any contractor personnel performing service on site at the VA brings parts, devices, or equipment that have serial numbers and will be used in patient care, these items must be checked in upon entry and checked out upon exiting the VA with both Logistics and Biomed departments. Shipment: Contractor shall be responsible for shipment of repair parts and substitute equipment at no expense to the government, with FOB destination terms applicable in these circumstances, and in favor of the VA Medical Center at this location. All shipments, labels, invoices and correspondence related to this contract must include the contract number and marked Attn: COR/Local VA POC [insert individual name] . Contractor must email the local VA POC or COR with carrier and tracking information in advance of all shipment of parts and equipment so the VA may be prepared to receive the items and track them to avoid loss. GOVERNMENT FURNISHED EQUIPMENT / PROPERTY (GFE / GFP) Government Property is any real property at the VAMC accessed by the Contractor in the performance of services in accordance with the PWS. Condition of Equipment The Contractor shall accept responsibility for the equipment in "as is" condition. Failure to inspect the equipment prior to contract award shall not relieve the Contractor from performance of the requirements of this contract. Storage Storage for Contractor equipment is not provided at the VAMC. The Contractor is responsible for the security of its equipment. The Government is not responsible for the security of Contractor equipment. CONTRACTOR FURNISHED EQUIPMENT / PROPERTY (CFE / CFP) Service Manuals/Tools/Equipment The VAMC shall not provide tools, (test) equipment, service manuals or service diagnostic software to the contractor. The contractor shall obtain, have on file, and make available to its FSE's all operational and technical documentation (such as; operational and service manuals, schematics, and parts list) which are necessary to meet the performance requirements of this contract. The location and listing of the service data manuals, by name and/or the manuals themselves shall be provided to the CO upon request.

title: GOCO Industry Day
description: Executive Summary The current operating strategy for Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) Army ammunition plants requires reassessment to ensure the Organic Industrial Base can meet future requirements for safety, responsiveness, capacity, modernization, supply-chain resilience, and affordable lifecycle performance. Traditional GOCO competition and contract approaches may not consistently create the incentives, flexibility, or accountability necessary to operate Government-owned facilities as modern and competitive manufacturing enterprises. In particular, existing approaches may overemphasize Government-directed workload and reimbursed facility operations rather than operator responsibility for productive utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce development, workload capture, and operational performance. The Government is seeking industry input on a commercially disciplined GOCO operating model that preserves Government mission priorities while providing the operating contractor meaningful responsibility and flexibility to manage the facility as a competitive manufacturing enterprise. Under such a model, the contractor would be expected to sustain, modernize, maintain, and improve the facility through efficient operations, productive utilization, pursuit of approved workload, and sound business practices. The Government seeks to identify contracting, workload, risk-allocation, facility-use, oversight, intellectual-property, and performance-management constructs that will enable this model while preserving appropriate Government accountability, safety, security, and access to required production capacity. Portfolio Acquisition Executive Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE AS&A) is assessing the future GOCO operating strategy before proceeding with future GOCO competitions. Purpose Army Contracting Command � Rock Island, on behalf of PAE AS&A, intends to host an Industry Day in November 2026 focused on transforming the operating strategy for GOCO Army ammunition plants. Specific Industry Day details will be provided separately; registration is not currently required. This Request for Information (RFI), together with the subsequent Industry Day, will help the Government understand feasible business and operating models for future GOCO facilities. The Government will use industry feedback to inform discussion of alternative approaches to facility operations, modernization, workload management, contract structure, and oversight. Objective The Government�s objective is to establish a commercially disciplined operating model for GOCO Army ammunition plants that improves responsiveness to Warfighter requirements while sustaining long-term plant viability, modernization, competitiveness, and accountability. The desired model would provide the operating contractor with appropriate flexibility and meaningful responsibility to manage facility utilization, maintenance, modernization, workforce, supply chain, and approved workload. The Government seeks input on the risk-allocation mechanisms, workload authorities, facility-use structures, performance measures, and oversight approaches necessary to support this model while preserving Government mission priorities. The desired end state is a modern, flexible production enterprise capable of efficiently increasing, reducing, pausing, restarting, changing over, and surging production in response to Warfighter need without disproportionate impacts to cost, schedule, quality, workforce readiness, safety, or production capability. The Government is particularly interested in performance measures that demonstrate: Safe and reliable operations; Schedule reliability and order-to-delivery responsiveness; Plant availability and production throughput; Rapid changeover, shutdown, restart, and surge capability; Flexible, modular, dual-use, and/or automated manufacturing capacity; Effective maintenance, workforce, and supply-chain management; Competitive lifecycle cost and productive utilization; Modernization outcomes that improve operating performance; and Appropriate transparency and accountability without unnecessary Government direction of day-to-day operations. Areas of Consideration The Government developed the attached questionnaire based on the following interconnected areas of consideration. Respondents are requested to complete the associated questionnaire and provide practical recommendations, examples, and lessons learned from relevant commercial, defense-industrial, or other manufacturing environments. The Government is particularly interested in responses that: Describe a complete and coherent commercial operating model rather than isolated contractual changes; Identify recommended Government and contractor responsibilities; Explain the proposed allocation of risk and opportunity; Identify measurable outcomes and recommended key performance indicators; Describe the conditions necessary to modernize facilities and maintain flexible production capacity; Address how the model would operate during high-demand, low-demand, shutdown, restart, and surge conditions; Identify legal, regulatory, technical, security, safety, qualification, or business constraints requiring further Government consideration; and Contain data that supports its recommended solutions. 1. Commercial Operating Model and Risk Allocation The Government seeks input on operating models in which the contractor manages a Government-owned facility with commercial discipline while meeting Government mission priorities. Topics may include: Operator responsibilities, decision rights, and accountability; Allocation of demand, utilization, revenue, operating-cost, maintenance, modernization, obsolescence, and performance risk; Contractor responsibility for productive utilization and continuous improvement; Mechanisms that encourage modernization as an operating outcome rather than a discrete facility-improvement project; Gain-sharing, profit-sharing, retained earnings, or reinvestment approaches; Treatment of contractor-funded improvements at contract transition; and Protection of Government interests while maintaining meaningful contractor performance and market risk. 2. Demand, Capacity, and Workload Management The Government seeks input on how Government requirements and approved non-Government workload can be integrated to improve plant utilization, responsiveness, and long-term viability. Topics may include: Government demand forecasting and demand-signal quality; Government mission-priority requirements; Capacity reservation, surge, turn-down, shutdown, restart, and reconstitution; Minimum Government commitments, if necessary, and the appropriate purpose and scope of such commitments; Integration of Government, commercial, Foreign Military Sales, and other approved workload; Multi-year procurement and workload-planning approaches; Workforce retention and readiness during periods of variable demand; and Mechanisms for balancing Government access to capacity with contractor responsibility for utilization. 3. Modern, Flexible, and Resilient Production The Government seeks concepts for modernizing GOCO production capability to improve agility, resilience, and efficient response to changing demand. Topics may include: Flexible, modular, dual-use, and automated production lines; Rapid product changeover and qualification; Planned shutdown, restart, and surge capability; Automation, robotics, digital manufacturing, digital twins, and predictive maintenance; Equipment replacement, facility renewal, and obsolescence management; Workforce cross-training and critical-skill retention; Supply-chain resilience and access to existing U.S. industrial capacity; and Technical, regulatory, contractual, qualification, or facility barriers that limit modernization and flexibility. 4. title: Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) Call for Whitepapers for Mission Development Zone (MDZ) Outgrant
description: ** The response due date has been extended from 2 October 2026 to 16 October 2026** 1. DESCRIPTION 1.1. Growth of the U.S. Domestic Space industry has resulted in a greater demand for use of real property at U.S. Space Force (USSF) Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30), Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) by private and commercial entities to conduct spaceport support, payload processing, hardware manufacturing, testing, logistics, and other space-related activities. Ensuring that United States operators can efficiently process space systems, conduct missions in space, launch, and reenter United States airspace is critical to economic growth, national security, and accomplishing Federal space objectives. 1.2. SLD 30 requests white paper responses from United States Commercial Providers as defined by 51 U.S.C. � 50101(7) engaged in space transportation, spaceport support, spacecraft manufacturing, payload processing, assembly, test, space logistics, or other space-related operations on the buildout of the Mission Development Zone (MDZ). Respondents will offer insights, perspectives, and approaches to obtain real property-use agreements to finance, design, construct, operate, and maintain spaceport infrastructure. Industry insights from whitepaper submissions may be utilized to drive future RFI / RFP announcements issued by SLD 30. Specifically, the MDZ infrastructure is intended to provide critical support services to the Department of War (DoW), commercial spaceflight, and other spaceport users at an undeveloped area located in the southern region of VSFB�s North Base area. Development and utilization of the MDZ will be in support of maximizing spaceport capability and assured access to space to achieve national security objectives. 1.3. Description of Premises is at Exhibit B. Please note that the MDZ is not a space launch complex (launch pad), but rather a flexible development zone dedicated to supporting the broader spaceport ecosystem. This includes, but is not limited to, payload processing, hazardous processing, spaceport logistics, commodity storage, launch and mission control, research and development, spacecraft integration, and administrative/engineering spaces. 1.4. The USSF is gathering market intelligence to determine the feasibility of a future real property outgrant under 10 U.S.C. � 2667 to a commercial space services provider, spaceport support provider, launch service provider (LSP), space infrastructure provider, or other space-related entity to construct spaceport-related support infrastructure. MDZ support infrastructure may include, but is not limited to, the following activities: processing, manufacturing, logistics, and administrative support activities. Data gathered from white paper responses will directly inform the Government in determining optimal MDZ utilization and potential infrastructure requirements to meet Government and industry launch requirements. 1.5. To support its ongoing spaceport capacity expansion, Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30) continuously evaluates opportunities and fields requests for new missions. Accordingly, SLD 30 provides discretionary site access and information to prospective partners at any time. Spaceport users and providers responding to this call for whitepapers wishing to view the site may request a property viewing. Please note that scheduling a site visit does not constitute grounds for extending the submittal deadline. 2. CONDITIONS 2.1. This call for whitepapers is not governed by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and is not a Request for Information (RFI), a Request for Proposal (RFP), a Request for Quote (RFQ), nor a solicitation announcement. Content of whitepapers will provide industry insight to assist the Government in scoping, planning, and defining requirements for the proposed MDZ. Content of the whitepapers may assist the Government in generating future contract requirements. Submitters agree and allow the USSF to use the information in the submissions for this purpose. 2.2. This call for whitepapers is issued solely for informational and planning purposes, and the Government is under no obligation to allocate property. The information contained herein is current as of the publication date but subject to change; it is not binding and may be amended in the future. While SLD 30 intends to review submissions, it is under no obligation to do so and reserves the right to cancel or amend the call for whitepapers at its sole discretion. 2.3. No funds are available to fund the whitepaper requested and the Government will not pay or reimburse any costs associated with responding to this request. 2.4. Any future facility where energetic propellants, hazardous materials, and/or ordnance will be used, processed, or stored will require the development of an explosives site plan. To assist the Government in layout and zoning analysis, respondents should outline any anticipated explosive safety arcs, quantity-distance (QD) requirements, or specialized hazard mitigation constraints. 3. PURPOSE & OBJECTIVES Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF), under contracting activity N4523A, is conducting market research to: Assess Commercial & Modified COTS Availability: Determine whether commercial products currently available in the commercial marketplace�or commercial products that can be modified of a type customarily available in the commercial marketplace to meet the Government's requirement�satisfy PSNS & IMF's operational parameters pursuant to RFO FAR Part 12. Evaluate Customary Commercial Practices & Customary Modifications: In accordance with RFO FAR Subpart 12.1 (Pre-solicitation), identify commercial practices regarding warranties, maintenance intervals, testing, and delivery terms, and understand the degree of adaptation required to configure commercial industrial nitrogen plants into shipyard-ready, containerized units. Obtain Specification Feedback: Solicit industry input, risk assessments, and recommendations regarding the Government's draft performance requirements to eliminate overly restrictive or non-commercial specifications. Refine Acquisition Strategy: Gauge market maturity, delivery lead times, First Article Test (FAT) feasibility, and cost drivers to structure an optimal commercial IDIQ solicitation under streamlined RFO FAR Part 12 procedures. 3. CONTEMPLATED CONTRACT STRUCTURE & SCOPE The Government is contemplating an Indefinite Delivery / Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract structure utilizing FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services) streamlined procedures in conjunction with FAR Part 15 (Contracting by Negotiation): Item Categorization: Modified Commercial Product. The baseline generation system must rely on active production commercial products and components with active commercial part-numbers; prototype or unproven "pre-production" components are not authorized. First Article Test (FAT) Unit: Two (2) initial units subject to qualification, Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory (NRTL) inspection, independent accredited laboratory gas purity verification, and operational verification testing. Lowest Price Technically Acceptable in accordance with FAR Part 15, where the lowest price meeting or exceeding the acceptability standards for non-cost factors. 4. See attached Draft Statement of Work. 5. Does your product qualify as a "Commercial Product" or a "Commercial Product with Modifications" under FAR 2.101? What specific modifications would be required to adapt your standard commercial offering to meet the PSNS specifications (e.g., ISO container integration, shipyard color restrictions, specific alarm announcements, acoustic attenuation)? Are these modifications of a type customarily available in the commercial marketplace? What are standard commercial warranty terms, customary commercial maintenance agreements, and commercial service intervals for equipment of this type? Under RFO FAR Part 12, what standard commercial terms and conditions or financing practices should the Government consider incorporating or tailoring? Topic B: Technical Feasibility, Packaging, & Trade-offs Is packaging the complete system within a single ISO container achievable using mature, non-developmental COTS components? If bottle banks or compressors require external placement or a two-container configuration, what are the primary engineering trade-offs (e.g., thermal management, footprint, mobilization time)? What technology type (e.g., multi-stage Pressure Swing Adsorption [PSA], catalytic deoxo purification, hybrid membrane/cryogenic) do you recommend to reliably achieve under fluctuating shipyard demand cycles? Does the requirement for 7-day autonomous operation present any unforeseen failure modes or safety hazards in an unmanned industrial outdoor yard setting? What lead time is expected for follow-on production delivery orders (e.g., 1�3 units per order)? What are the primary cost and schedule drivers in the draft requirements (e.g., purity verification, acoustic attenuations, marine coating, 180-day continuous run requirement)? Under the contemplated FAR Part 12 / Part 15 Best Value Tradeoff framework, what commercial evaluation factors (e.g., past performance, demonstrated commercial reliability, warranty terms, life-cycle costs) would best enable offerors to propose innovative commercial solutions? 6. title: INVITATION TO SUBMIT AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) AS TO THE AVAILABILITY OF SPACE FOR LEASE IN THE CITY OF COWANSVILLE (QUEBEC)
description: INVITATION TO SUBMIT AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) AS TO THE AVAILABILITY OF SPACE FOR LEASE IN THE CITY OF COWANSVILLE (QUEBEC) FILE NUMBER: 81003487 Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately fifteen (15) years, commencing on or about March 1, 2029; • approximately six hundred nineteen (619) usable square meters (um2) of contiguous office space. • the proposed space must be available approximately twenty-four (24) weeks prior to the above-noted lease commencement date so all space(s) may be prepared for occupancy; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. The proposed space should be contiguous, unobstructed, preferably on the ground floor, although premises located on the second floor could be considered. The Lessee may also consider offices located on a maximum of two contiguous floors including the ground floor and second floor; 2. The proposed building must have a window arrangement and configuration that are acceptable to the lessee; 3. the proposed space should be within an office or commercial building; industrial type buildings and those with industrial space will not be considered; 4. The physical characteristics of the sites and buildings, as well as the use of neighboring land and the surrounding area must be compatible with the intended use; 5. The building where the premises will be located must be fully accessible to everyone, integrating physical, sensory, and cognitive needs; 6. The space must be accessible by public transport; 7. The availability of 15 visitors parking spaces within 500 meters walking distance to be calculated from the building entrance closest to the potential office space using only sidewalks, pedestrian crosswalks and pedestrian paths; ? the proposed space must be located in the city of Cowansville, province of Quebec, and the geographical boundaries exclude agricultural, industrial, and residential areas. Mixed-use real estate zones or project (residential and commercial) could be considered. • on or before the lease commencement date, the proposed space will have to comply with all requirements contained in PSPC’s Standards for Leased Accommodation, a copy of which may be obtained from the contact listed in Section F; Note: PSPC may wish to visit or inspect the proposed space upon reasonable notice and a threat and risk assessment may be undertaken in order to assess potential threats to the security of the proposed space and to the public. Section B: Responses Interested parties are requested to submit their response to this EOI in writing to the following address: Public Services and Procurement Canada Place Bonaventure, South-West Portal 800, de la Gauchetière St West, suite 7300 Montréal (Québec) H5A 1L6 or by email to the contact listed below in Section F. Please indicate File No. 81003487 on all correspondence. Section C: Responses Requested by As this may be the only invitation to submit an Expression of Interest for this potential lease project, owners/mandatories should provide their response by October 16, 2026. Any response received after this date may not be considered. Section D: Information Provided by Interested Parties or Mandatories of Interested Parties Information provided by interested parties or mandatories of interested parties should include the file number, the location and municipal address of the building, current zoning, specific location of space within the building, measured area of space, architectural drawings identifying the proposed space with washrooms, exits and other design elements, and details addressing the criteria listed above in Section A. Mandatories submitting a response to this EOI must provide PSPC with a letter authorizing them to do so. Section E: Security Requirement If this EOI results in a future tender process, the building owners of the proposed spaces will have to hold a valid security clearance at the “Reliability” level, approved and granted by the Canadian Industrial Security Directorate (CISD) of PSPC prior to the beginning of the fit up work. All parties interested in this potential lease project are advised to obtain this security clearance level in advance. Information regarding security clearance can be obtained on the website of the CISD/ PSPC at http://ssi-iss.tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca. Please contact the person listed in Section F to initiate the security clearance process. Section F: Additional Information For more information, please contact Aubray Roy, Senior Leasing Officer by phone at 438-465-0428 or by email to: aubray.roy@tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca. Section G: List of Available Space This EOI is issued in order to invite interested parties to demonstrate their interest in providing the requirements described herein. This information may be included in a list of available space and used for potential future solicitations. Section H: Not a Solicitation Process Note that this is not a tender process, nor a request for proposal, but only an inquiry as to the availability of space to lease. PSPC will not necessarily invite offers, or lease any space, and may not post any future ads related to this request. The information provided through this EOI may be included in a source list of available space and PSPC may issue an invitation to tender for other leasing requirements based on this information, or based on any other information which may come to its attention prior to an issuance of an invitation to tender; or it may invite offers by way of public tender. PSPC reserves the right to proceed with an Invitation to Offer to Lease by inviting only parties deemed to most effectively meet specific operational, security and public safety requirements.

title: JOFOC for Data Analysis for Quality, Safety & Oversight of the ESRD, Transplant, and OPO Programs
description: The contractor will provide detailed data reports about End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) facilities (commonly referred to as dialysis facilities), Transplant Programs, and Organ Procurement Organizations (OPOs) in formats that are useful to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), states, health care providers, and the general public. These reports will include summaries of patient characteristics, facility characteristics, patient outcomes, and facility practice patterns. These reports will include comparative state, network, regional, and national statistics as appropriate. These reports will be used by CMS in overseeing the quality and safety of the ESRD, Transplant and OPO Programs. For the Dialysis Facility Reports (DFRs), the contractor will use data from a variety of sources to create summary reports to be used to provide Federal, state and facility oversight of dialysis facilities. Data from all available sources, including the CMS Central Data Repository (CDR), claims forms, eligibility forms, clinical data sources, facility inventories, death forms, and survey and certification forms will be updated, edited, validated, and utilized by the contractor to create a series of reports that will assist CMS, states, and other entities in monitoring the care provided by ESRD facilities. These reports will be risk-adjusted and facility, state, regional, and corporate-specific for each fiscal year. The reports shall include a rank-ordered Outcomes List of ESRD facilities for each state. The Outcomes Lists will be constructed from a composite of data elements that most validly and reliably identify facilities with potential problems. The contractor will routinely revise the DFRs to ensure they are 1) aligned with the ESRD Survey process, 2) provide development of data sources and data tools to allow state surveyors convenient and timely access to more current dialysis facility quality outcomes, 3) use state surveyor and other DFR user feedback to determine the need for revisions. The contractor will provide guidance on using advanced technologies and incorporate plans to integrate emerging technologies associated with Electronic Health Records (EHRs). The contractor will prepare Transplant Program reports and OPO reports. The data for these reports will be obtained from the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) of the Health Resources and Services Agency (HRSA), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and Multiple Cause of Death (MCOD) databases. This data will be used in the calculation of annual OPO performance measure scores as required by the CMS regulations at 42 CFR �486.318.

title: General Contractor for the Seismic Retrofit Project at the Clemente Ruiz Nazario U.S. Courthouse, San Juan, Puerto Rico
description: THIS IS A SYNOPSIS/PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY. This notice is not a request for offers or proposals. This notice does not represent a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service, Acquisition Project Delivery � Capital Construction Division, intends to solicit for a highly qualified Contractor who can provide Construction Services to perform a Seismic Retrofit at the Clemente Ruiz Nazario U.S. Courthouse (Nazario Courthouse) located at 150 Carlos Chardon Avenue in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Nazario Courthouse will remain fully operational throughout the duration of the Seismic Retrofit. To ensure minimal disruption to Government operations, the work will predominantly be executed after business hours. The selected General Contractor will be required to ensure full compliance with the Government�s requirements for access and security. Additionally, the General Contractor will be required to complete this project in accordance with the construction drawings and specifications that will be issued for this project. Contract Type: The contract type for this procurement will be Firm-Fixed price. The line item schedule will include a lump sum item for the Base and Options. Price: The total magnitude of this project at award is between $40,000,000 and $50,000,000. Selection and Schedule: The General Contractor will be selected through a procurement method developed in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation (Class Deviation RFO-2025-15) and FAR 36 Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-36). The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Evaluation process. During Phase I, prospective firms must submit technical qualifications detailing their experience with comparable efforts and previous records of past-performance. In Phase II, selected General Contractors shall demonstrate their operational strategy and planned subcontracting framework. Evaluation of Phase II technical submissions will be conducted in full before the Government reviews the price proposal. GSA anticipates award of a contract for these services in August 2027. The period of performance for the proposed contract will be for approximately forty six (46) months upon issuance of notice to proceed. NAICS: This procurement will be conducted under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 236220--Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Small Business size standard is an average annual sales and receipts for the past three (3) years that are equal to or less than $45,000,000. Solicitation Information: GSA anticipates issuing the Solicitation on or about October 19, 2026, with receipt of Phase I proposals due at a minimum of forty-five (45) calendar days later. All information, amendments and questions concerning this solicitation will be electronically posted to the Government-wide Point of Entry at www.SAM.gov. No telephone requests will be accepted and no paper copies will be mailed to prospective offerors. A bid guarantee (bid bond) will be required at twenty (20) percent of the bid price or $3 million, whichever is less, at the time of Phase II proposal submission. Upon contract award, both the Performance and Payment bonds will be required at 100% of the total contract value. Any firms unable to meet the bond requirements will be ineligible for a contract award. All offerors are required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (www.SAM.gov) at the time of offer submission, and shall continue to be registered until time of award, during performance and through final payment of the contract. In addition, in order for contractors to have access to Federal space, the contractor will be required to adhere to the Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12), Directive Clearance Process, in accordance with FAR 52.204-9 - Personal Identity Verification of Contractor Personnel (JAN 2011) as well as other security clearances that may be required.

title: Y1DA--561A4-23-101 Replace Hot Water Heaters
description: Presolicitation Notice Presolicitation Notice Page 4 of 4 Presolicitation Notice *=Required Field Presolicitation Notice Page 1 of 4 This notice is for Solicitation Number 36C24226B0052, Project Number 561A4-23-101 Replace Multiple Building s Water Heaters at the VA Health Care System, Lyons Campus, 151 Knollcroft Rd., Lyons, NJ 07939-5001. This shall be a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Set-Aside. As a result, all SDVOSB's may submit a bid, which will be considered by the agency. This project is classified under NAICS Code 238220 and has a size standard of $19 Million. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. Scope of Work: The scope of work shall generally consist of, but not limited to the following: The project involves upgrading the Hot Water Heater system (specifically Buildings 3, 7, 53, 54, and 143 and their associated mechanical and utility spaces). The existing domestic hot water heating systems at the Lyons VA Medical Center consist of aging tank type and semi-instantaneous water heaters and associated recirculation pumps that are inefficient, and beyond their intended service life. These units serve critical patient care, residential, and support areas and must be upgraded to meet current VA design standards, energy efficiency requirements, and plumbing and electrical codes while maintaining continuous hot water service to the occupied facility. The water heaters shall be replaced sequentially so that only one unit is taken out of service at a given time, and the others remain in full operation. This approach will ensure continuous domestic hot water service to the building throughout construction, with at least one operational hot water heater. Replacing these units will significantly reduce maintenance time, improve system control and enhance the distribution of hot water across rooms, floors, and departments. The contractor shall completely prepare site for building operations, including demolishing selected existing water heaters, recirculation pumps, and associated steam, condensate, and domestic water piping and furnish and install new semi-instantaneous steam to hot water heaters, recirculation pumps, condensate receiver/pump, piping, insulation, electrical feeders, disconnects, and controls as indicated in the 100% construction documents. Work also includes startup, testing, balancing, commissioning and training the VA plumbing staff on the new equipment. The contractor shall also furnish all labor, materials, tool, and supervision necessary to perform work for VA Project 561A4-23-101 Replace Multiple Building s Water Heaters, in accordance with AE drawings and specifications. Project Completion: 180 Calendar Days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). All other details and information shall be contained in the solicitation which shall be posted on www.sam.gov. The solicitation will be released on or about July 20, 2026. The response submittal address, date and time will be included in the solicitation. This project requires bonding and all responses/submissions to the solicitation to be posted later shall be emailed. No hand-carried bids will be accepted. All prospective bidders must be currently registered in www.sam.gov , and be registered and verified as a Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) in https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ at the time of offer submission and before award of this procurement.
